questions.stem: The Latin root 'port' means 'to carry'. What exactly does the word 'portable' mean?

options.option_text: A very large, permanently fixed, unmovable physical building.
Able to be easily carried or moved from one place to another.
A completely invisible gaseous substance. (alternative interpretation)
An object that has been completely destroyed. (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: 'Portable' combines 'port' (carry) and '-able' (capable of). It describes something that is designed to be easily carried.

questions.stem: Combining the prefix 'im-' (into) and the root 'port' (carry), what does 'import' exactly mean in trade?

options.option_text: To destroy all locally produced domestic goods. (alternative interpretation)
To give away free products to poor local farmers.
To bring goods or services into a country from abroad for sale.
To stop all international trading immediately. (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: To 'import' means to bring (goods or services) into a country from abroad for sale. It literally means 'carry into'.

questions.stem: Combining the prefix 'ex-' (out) and the root 'port', what does 'export' exactly mean?

options.option_text: To buy products exclusively from foreign companies.
To refuse to sell local items completely. (alternative interpretation)
To permanently close a large trading harbor.
To send goods or services to another country for sale.

questions.explanation: To 'export' means to send (goods or services) to another country for sale. It literally means 'carry out'.

questions.stem: The prefix 'trans-' means 'across'. What exactly does 'transport' fundamentally mean?

options.option_text: To take or carry people or goods from one place to another.
To quickly change a person's physical appearance completely.
To translate a foreign language into a local dialect.
To suddenly disappear without any prior warning.

questions.explanation: To 'transport' means to take or carry (people or goods) from one place to another. It translates literally to 'carry across'.

questions.stem: What exactly is a 'portfolio' in the context of the root word 'port'?

options.option_text: A massive ocean vessel used exclusively for military transport. (alternative interpretation)
A tiny digital storage device holding musical tracks. (alternative interpretation)
A large, thin, flat case used for carrying loose sheets of paper, drawings, or maps.
A specialized musical instrument that is very difficult to play. (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: A 'portfolio' (from 'portare' to carry + 'foglio' leaf/sheet) is a flat case for carrying loose sheets of paper, or metaphorically a range of investments or pieces of work.

questions.stem: The prefix 'de-' means 'away'. In law, what exactly does it mean to 'deport' someone?

options.option_text: To warmly welcome a new political refugee legally.
To officially expel a foreigner from a country.
To formally grant immediate national citizenship to a foreigner.
To quietly hire a foreign worker for a highly skilled job.

questions.explanation: To 'deport' means to officially expel a foreigner from a country. It translates directly to 'carry away'.

questions.stem: The prefix 'com-' means 'with'. What exactly does the formal word 'comport' mean?

options.option_text: To legally quickly cancel a previously signed legal contract.
To physically comfort a crying or deeply upset child.
To forcefully forcefully break down a heavily locked thick door.
To conduct oneself or behave in a particular manner.

questions.explanation: To 'comport' oneself means to conduct oneself or behave in a particular manner. It literally means 'to carry oneself with'.
